historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward-looking build, not a trailing CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Trailing CAGRs are not usable as a forward proxy here and are reported for completeness only. The 5yr revenue CAGR (24.0%) is inflated by the FY2021-23 NBN construction/HFC-decommissioning volume spike (revenue nearly doubled FY21->FY22 on lower-margin project work, EBITDA margin collapsed to 1.7% and the company booked a $38.2m impairment); the 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is negative only because FY2026 capex tripled for one-off Defence fleet mobilisation and cash tax included a one-off prior-year catch-up (see inputs.notes). None of these describe the business today. The base-case growth path is instead built bottom-up from the Defence contract's full-year run-rate (see assumptions.base.narrative) plus RiE Group, against continued Telecommunications softness -- selected_growth_rate (6.0%, FY27) is that estimate, not a CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: Defence ramps to a full year, RiE adds a small bolt-on, Telco keeps softening moderately while Utilities keeps expanding margin -- net mid-single-digit growth decelerating to a 2.5% terminal rate, EBITDA margin maturing at ~7.8%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Defence becomes a genuine second growth pillar, further bolt-on M&A repeats the RiE template, Telco stabilises instead of shrinking, and Utilities margin expansion continues past FY2026's pace -- margin matures near 9%.
scenario_narratives.bear: NBN/Telstra/Optus concentration bites (the BSA precedent), Defence mobilisation disappoints on margin, and competitive government tendering caps the margin story -- growth stalls near zero for several years before a modest recovery.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Service Stream is a thin-margin, government/carrier-counterparty infrastructure services contractor with a net-cash, zero-debt balance sheet, record work-in-hand and a genuine but early-stage diversification (Defence, industrials/energy-transition bolt-ons) away from its historically NBN/telco-dependent revenue base. The owner-FCF DCF values it on a component build off statutory revenue and EBITDA-from-Operations margin, with the FY2026 base year explicitly normalised for a one-off tax-payment catch-up and a Defence-mobilisation capex spike so the terminal path is not anchored to either extreme.
key_risks_to_valuation: Customer/segment concentration: Telecommunications (NBN Co, Telstra, Optus) is still 43% of group revenue and the BSA precedent shows how fast that can unwind
Defence base-services is a brand-new vertical for the company (only 5 months of FY2026 trading) -- the margin and retention profile is unproven beyond initial mobilisation
Thin group EBITDA margin (6.6-7.0%) leaves little buffer against wage/subcontractor cost inflation or re-tender pricing pressure on ~70%-government-linked revenue

FY2026 capex and cash tax were both one-off elevated (Defence fleet mobilisation; FY2025 tax installment catch-up) -- getting the normalisation wrong in either direction materially moves the valuation
Working capital/cash conversion has swung meaningfully in the past (H1 FY2022/23) despite FY2026's strong 113.9% conversion

inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted weighted average from FY2026 EPS note (625,902k); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Only real on-market buyback in the company's history was FY2018 ($8.0m); 'Purchase of shares' in other years ($13.0m FY2026) is treasury-share funding for employee equity plans, not a capital return, and is excluded from buyback_cash.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement add-back, 'Equity-settled share-based payments' $5.053m (line 4734/5846 of the annual report). No separate equity-award-tax withholding line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes KPI is 0 across the full history) so the cash-flow add-back is the full charge.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T04:51:05Z regular session (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 1.78-2.72
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% built on AUD risk-free rate (~4.2% 10yr ACGB) plus an equity risk premium appropriate to an unlevered (net cash, zero drawn debt), ~70%-government-counterparty essential-infrastructure services contractor. Lower than a typical industrial given the annuity-style, government/regulated-utility revenue base (~80% of work-in-hand is O&M not project/construction) and zero financial leverage; not as low as a regulated utility given contract re-tender and customer-concentration risk (NBN Co/Telstra/Optus).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B (leases as operating cost). IFRS-16 lease PRINCIPAL ($30.310m FY2026) sits in financing activities and is deducted from reported OCF/FCF to reach owner FCF; lease INTEREST ($5.507m FY2026, inside 'Interest and facility costs paid' of $8.812m) is already an operating-activities outflow embedded in reported OCF, so it is not double-deducted. Forward-year lease cost is modelled explicitly as `lease_cost_pct_path` (principal+interest as % of revenue, ~1.4-1.5% of revenue, roughly flat) so the DCF's own EBITDA-from-Operations-style margin line is charged for it once. D&A in the component build is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation ($27.32m of the $59.15m FY2026 total, i.e. 1.16% of revenue) -- ROU depreciation is not separately charged again since the lease line already carries the full IFRS-16 cash cost. total_debt/net_debt EXCLUDE lease liabilities ($110.15m FY2026), consistent with treatment B.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- Service Stream has no minority interests; equity-accounted joint ventures (Transport Connect Sydney, others) are proportionately reflected via the 'Total Revenue including JV' vs statutory revenue reconciliation, and this model uses statutory (consolidated, ex-JV-share) revenue and cash flows throughout to keep the flows tied to what is actually collectable and bankable by the parent.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF via the engine route (dcf-methods SKILL.md routing table -- services/infrastructure operating company, most comparable row to 'industrial/cyclical operating company'). No prior DCF or memory entry exists for this ticker; this is a fresh build. FY2026 is NOT used as a clean base year for cash tax or capex: (a) cash tax paid $48.8m included a $26m one-off catch-up of the FY2025 final tax installment against an income-statement effective tax rate of a clean 25% both years, so the cash tax rate path ramps toward 25% rather than anchoring on the abnormal FY2026 cash figure; (b) net capex nearly tripled to $29.7m (0.96% of net-capex-to-revenue vs 0.38% FY2025) purely for Defence-contract fleet mobilisation, a step-up that is modelled as partially persisting (ongoing fleet renewal) rather than either the low FY2025 rate or the elevated FY2026 mobilisation rate. FY2022 is excluded from the historical margin/CAGR base -- statutory NPAT was a $36.3m loss on a $38.2m impairment; the company's own EBITDA-from-Operations ex-significant-items ($91.1m FY2022, $114.1m FY2023, $129.2m FY2024, $146.1m FY2025, $163.4m FY2026, Annual Report Table 13) is the clean underlying series used for margin trend. FY2023 cash tax was a $44.5m refund, also excluded as a base-year anchor.
inputs.wc_capture_rationale: Working capital is modelled near-neutral (small negative capture) rather than a meaningful tailwind or drag: Service Stream is a services contractor billing on progress/milestone terms with receivables and unbilled revenue broadly offsetting payables and provisions across the cycle: FY2026 cash conversion (OCFBIT) was 113.9%, i.e. working capital was a net source of cash this year, but the company's own risk disclosure flags historical swings (weak H1 FY2022/23 cash flow) so a structural positive capture is not assumed to repeat every year.

bear.narrative: Telecommunications concentration materialises as the sector's live tail risk -- peer BSA lost its NBN Unify contract and saw revenue collapse ~89%; a similar non-renewal or re-scoping of Service Stream's NBN/Telstra/Optus work (43% of group revenue) is not offset quickly enough by Defence and Utilities growth. Defence base-services mobilisation proves harder than expected (113 sites, ~350 new hires, new subcontractor relationships in an unfamiliar vertical) and margin on that contract disappoints in its scale-up years. Utilities and government tendering turns more competitive, capping the margin-expansion story at the current level rather than extending it, and wage/subcontractor cost inflation in a tight trades market erodes the thin (6-9% segment) margins further. Working capital swings recur (as seen in H1 FY2022/23) rather than the FY2026 cash-conversion strength persisting.

base.narrative: Defence base-services contract (only 5 months in FY2026, $87.9m revenue) runs a full 12 months in FY2027, adding an estimated ~$120-135m of incremental revenue at a run-rate similar to its five-month contribution; RiE Group (~$13m/yr) adds a further bolt-on. Telecommunications continues to soften modestly as NBN transition programs complete and 'Unify' O&M ramps more slowly than the programs it replaces; Utilities keeps expanding organically (water, energy transition) and its margin keeps improving on contract discipline and scale (4.5%->5.8% in FY2026 alone). Group EBITDA margin ramps from 6.95% (FY2026 actual, statutory revenue basis) toward a mature ~7.8% as Defence scales past mobilisation and Utilities margin gains continue, then holds -- reflecting a still-thin-margin, competitively-tendered government/carrier services business, not a structurally re-rating one. Growth decelerates from the Defence step-up toward a 2.5% terminal rate consistent with Australian population/GDP-linked infrastructure spend once the current contract-mix shift is digested.

bull.narrative: Defence base-services relationship expands beyond the initial 113 SA/NT sites (management flags it becoming 'a meaningful growth pillar'), the RiE Group bolt-on template is repeated with further complementary M&A funded from the net-cash balance sheet, and Utilities margin expansion continues past FY2026's pace as scale and productivity gains compound (energy-transition and water infrastructure investment cycle). Telecommunications stabilises rather than continuing to shrink as new NBN fibre-upgrade and Unify work ramps faster than the completing programs roll off. Record work-in-hand (~$15.5bn including extension options) converts at a higher rate than base case, and the ~93% contract-retention rate holds even as the book grows, letting group EBITDA margin reach ~9% -- still well short of a re-rating multiple, reflecting continued execution discipline rather than a change in the competitively-tendered, thin-margin nature of the business.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight held above the 15% house floor (at 25%) because customer concentration is a demonstrated, not theoretical, sector risk -- peer BSA's ~89% revenue collapse from losing its single NBN Unify contract happened in the same 2026 window this model is dated from, and Telecommunications is still 43% of Service Stream's group revenue. Bull weight trimmed to match (25%) because the bull case needs several independent things to go right (Defence scaling smoothly into a real second pillar, repeated accretive M&A, Telco stabilising rather than merely slowing) rather than one lever. Net cash balance sheet and ~93% contract retention argue against a still-heavier bear weight -- there is no going-concern or covenant risk here, only margin/growth-mix risk, which is why bear is 25% and not 35%+.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
